set_title: Surgery endings: -ectomy (cut out), -otomy (cut into), -ostomy (opening), -plasty (repair), -pexy (fix in place), -lysis (break down)
stem: A 2-month-old boy has antenatally detected hydronephrosis. Ultrasonography shows a dilated renal collecting system with a normal ureter and bladder. MAG3 shows delayed drainage and 30% function in that kidney, from obstruction at the ureteropelvic junction. Which procedure is indicated?
oneliner: 2-month-old boy, UPJ obstruction with delayed drainage, 30% function → which procedure?
ask: Which term names the indicated procedure?

whyNot.A: Removes the gallbladder; his problem is a **ureteropelvic junction obstruction**
whyNot.C: Cuts pyloric muscle; his problem is **kidney outflow obstruction**
whyNot.D: Opens the airway; his problem is **hydronephrosis**
whyNot.E: Fixes the testis in place; his problem is a **dilated collecting system**

why: Pyelo- (renal pelvis) + -plasty (reshape or repair): rebuilding the narrowed junction. **UPJ obstruction with delayed drainage and reduced function** needs it.

idea.rule: -plasty repairs or reshapes; Anderson-Hynes pyeloplasty fixes UPJ obstruction.
also: Most common cause of neonatal hydronephrosis

set_title: Fanconi anemia vs Fanconi syndrome and other aplasia names
stem: A 40-year-old man on long-term tenofovir has fatigue, bone pain and increased urination. Urine shows glucose and amino acids with a normal serum glucose. Serum phosphate and bicarbonate are low.
oneliner: 40-year-old man on tenofovir, bone pain + polyuria + glycosuria with normal glucose + low phosphate and bicarbonate → ?

whyNot.A: Fanconi anemia is a childhood marrow failure; he has **urinary glucose and low phosphate**
whyNot.B: Diamond-Blackfan anemia is an infant red-cell disease; he has **tubular losses of glucose, phosphate**
whyNot.C: Aplastic anemia causes pancytopenia; he has **glycosuria with normal serum glucose**
whyNot.E: Pure red cell aplasia causes anemia only; he has **low phosphate and bicarbonate**

why: Global failure of proximal tubule reabsorption: glucose, amino acids, phosphate, bicarbonate lost. **Glycosuria with normal glucose, low phosphate and acidosis**, here from tenofovir.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: inherited marrow failure, DNA repair defect

idea.rule: Fanconi syndrome: proximal tubule leak; check the drug list, especially tenofovir.
also: Also cystinosis, Wilson disease, heavy metals
